intended_object: Composition of morphisms in an S-linear category, viewed as an S-bilinear map Hom(X,Y) × Hom(Y,Z) → Hom(X,Z), (f, g) ↦ f ≫ g. Taken from the docstring and name.
explanation: The definition sends f to `leftComp S Z f`, the map g ↦ f ≫ g, so `comp X Y Z f g = f ≫ g`. Composition in a linear category is linear in each argument, and the two proofs check exactly that: linearity in g comes from `leftComp`, and the `map_add'`/`map_smul'` proofs give linearity in f. The definition asks S to be a commutative semiring. That is the standard requirement: a bilinear map is written as `M →ₗ[S] N →ₗ[S] P`, and for the inner space of linear maps to be an S-module again, S must be commutative. So this setting is the natural one. The definition is a local Mathlib definition, and no other Mathlib declaration defines the same object.
